tasks.title: Direct privileges of a role
tasks.statement: Output the direct privileges of the role app_rw: columns object, priv; ordered by object and privilege.
tasks.hint: A selection from grants by role.

tasks.title: Effective privileges with inheritance
tasks.statement: The role anna is a member of dev, dev of app_rw, and app_rw of report_ro. Output all privileges of anna, taking inheritance into account (no duplicates): object, priv; ordered by object and privilege.
tasks.hint: Collect the roles recursively: anna herself and all her ancestors, then select the privileges for those roles.

tasks.title: Who can delete
tasks.statement: Output the roles (name) that, taking inheritance into account, can perform DELETE on orders; ordered by name. Hint: check both the holders of the privilege themselves and those who are members of such roles.
tasks.hint: Go down the inheritance: members of the holder roles get the right too.
tasks.starter:
-- who can DELETE on orders
WITH RECURSIVE

tasks.title: Excessive privileges
tasks.statement: Output the roles that have the DROP privilege on any object although they are not owner: column role; ordered by name. Include privileges inherited through membership.
tasks.hint: Recursively collect the roles with DROP and those who are members of them; exclude owner.
tasks.starter:
-- roles with DROP, except owner
WITH RECURSIVE

tasks.title: GRANT as INSERT
tasks.statement: GRANT is modelled by an insert into grants. Give the role report_ro the SELECT privilege on users, and take the UPDATE privilege on orders away from app_rw (DELETE from grants). The result is checked against the grants table.
tasks.hint: One INSERT of a row and a DELETE with three conditions.

tasks.title: Row protection through a view
tasks.statement: Create a view people_a that shows only the people of tenant 'A' (all columns). The result is checked by selecting from the view by id.
tasks.hint: CREATE VIEW … AS SELECT * FROM people WHERE tenant = 'A'.
tasks.starter:
-- RLS via view
CREATE VIEW people_a AS

tasks.title: Only safe columns
tasks.statement: Create a view people_public(id, name, city) without email and phone. The result is checked by a selection and by the list of the view's columns.
tasks.hint: List only the permitted columns.
tasks.starter:
-- a safe view
CREATE VIEW people_public AS

tasks.title: Masking an email
tasks.statement: Output the masked email: the first letter + '***' + everything starting from the '@' character. Columns id, masked; ordered by id. Example: anna@mail.ru → a***@mail.ru.
tasks.hint: substr(email, 1, 1) and substr(email, instr(email, '@')).

tasks.title: Masking a phone number
tasks.statement: Output the last 4 characters of the phone number, replacing the rest with asterisks as a single group: '***' || the last 4. For NULL, NULL. Columns id, masked; ordered by id.
tasks.hint: substr(phone, -4) takes the last 4 characters; CASE for NULL.

tasks.title: Anonymization for tests
tasks.statement: Anonymize the table: name = 'User' || id, email = 'user' || id || '@example.com', phone = NULL. The result is checked against the table.
tasks.hint: One UPDATE with three assignments.
tasks.starter:
-- UPDATE for the test environment
UPDATE people

tasks.title: k-anonymity
tasks.statement: Groups by city with fewer than 2 people make it possible to identify a person. Output such cities and the number of people: columns city, n; ordered by city.
tasks.hint: GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) < 2.

tasks.title: Finding personal data
tasks.statement: Find the notes that contain an email address (they have the '@' character): column id; ascending.
tasks.hint: LIKE '%@%'.

tasks.title: The right to erasure
tasks.statement: At the request of a data subject, delete all data of the user with email 'a@x.ru' from all tables with a single DELETE command (the cascade does the rest). The result is checked against three tables.
tasks.hint: Cascading foreign keys will delete the dependent rows by themselves.
tasks.starter:
-- delete the data subject
DELETE FROM

tasks.title: Audit trigger
tasks.statement: Create a trigger trg_audit AFTER UPDATE OF balance ON accounts: it writes a row (acc_id, old_balance, new_balance) into audit. Then run UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 25 WHERE id = 1. The result is checked against audit.
tasks.hint: CREATE TRIGGER … AFTER UPDATE OF balance ON accounts BEGIN INSERT … VALUES (OLD.id, OLD.balance, NEW.balance); END;
tasks.starter:
-- audit of changes
CREATE TRIGGER trg_audit

tasks.title: Who changed the most
tasks.statement: For each user, output the number of DELETE actions: columns who, deletes; ordered by count descending, then by name. Only those who had any.
tasks.hint: WHERE action = 'DELETE' and GROUP BY who.

tasks.title: Password guessing
tasks.statement: Output the IP addresses from which there were 3 or more failed logins (ok = 0): columns ip, failures; ordered by count descending, then by address.
tasks.hint: WHERE ok = 0, GROUP BY ip, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.

tasks.title: Lockout after failures
tasks.statement: Output the users who, according to the log, have at least two failed logins and no successful ones: column user; ordered by name.
tasks.hint: GROUP BY user HAVING SUM(ok = 0) >= 2 AND SUM(ok = 1) = 0.

tasks.title: Suspicious queries in the log
tasks.statement: Find the records that contain signs of injection: the substrings ' OR 1=1' or '; DROP' (case does not matter, LIKE is enough). Column id; ascending.
tasks.hint: Two LIKEs joined with OR.
tasks.starter:
-- looking for traces of injections
SELECT

tasks.title: Salted password hash
tasks.statement: Write hash_password(password, salt): the result is hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password.encode(), salt.encode(), 1000).hex(), a string of hexadecimal digits. (The exact value matters for submission: the parameters are fixed.)
tasks.hint: hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', …, 1000).hex().

tasks.title: Password verification
tasks.statement: Write verify_password(password, salt, stored): True if hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password.encode(), salt.encode(), 1000).hex() matches stored. Compare in constant time (hmac.compare_digest).
tasks.hint: hmac.compare_digest(h, stored).

tasks.title: Password policy
tasks.statement: Rules: length at least 8 ('short'), contains a digit ('no-digit'), contains an uppercase letter ('no-upper'), no three identical characters in a row ('repeat'). Write password_violations(pw): a sorted list of the violated rules.
tasks.hint: Four independent checks; sort the result.

tasks.title: Parameterized query
tasks.statement: Only the tables users and orders are allowed, and the filter columns are id, name, city, status. Write build_query(table, filters): a pair [sql, params], where sql = 'SELECT * FROM <table> WHERE a = ? AND b = ?' (conditions in the order of the keys of the dict filters; with no filters, 'SELECT * FROM <table>'), and params are the values in the same order. If the table or a column is not allowed, return None.
tasks.hint: Allowlists for the table and the columns; values go only into params.

tasks.title: Safe sorting
tasks.statement: The user passes a column and a direction. Allowed are the columns from allowed and the directions 'asc'/'desc' (case-insensitive). Write safe_order_by(column, direction, allowed): the string 'ORDER BY col DIR' (direction in capitals) or 'ORDER BY id ASC' if the input is not allowed.
tasks.hint: Check both parameters against allowlists.

tasks.title: Suspicious input
tasks.statement: Write looks_like_injection(s): True if the lowercased string contains one of these signs: "' or ", "--", ";", "union select", "/*". Otherwise False. This is a heuristic for the log, not a defense.
tasks.hint: Convert to lowercase and check each substring.

tasks.title: Role inheritance
tasks.statement: Roles are given by a dict "role → list of parent roles", privileges by a dict "role → list of privileges". Write effective_privs(role, parents, privs): a sorted list of the role's privileges taking inheritance into account (cycles are allowed). Unknown roles have no privileges.
tasks.hint: Traverse the role graph with a set of visited roles.

tasks.title: Row policy
tasks.statement: Rows are dicts with the key 'tenant'. Write rls_filter(rows, tenant, is_owner): if is_owner, all rows (the owner bypasses the policy), otherwise only the tenant's rows.
tasks.hint: A list with a filter by tenant, or without it for the owner.

tasks.title: Masking a card number
tasks.statement: Write mask_card(number): keep the last 4 digits, replace the other digits with '•', and keep spaces and hyphens as they are. If there are fewer than 4 digits, keep all the digits.
tasks.hint: Find the positions of the digits; keep the last 4.

tasks.title: Small groups
tasks.statement: Records are lists of quasi-identifier values (for example, [city, age]). Write small_groups(rows, k): a sorted list of groups (as lists) that occur fewer than k times.
tasks.hint: Count the tuples and select the groups with n < k.

tasks.title: What changed
tasks.statement: The rows before and after are dicts. Write audit_diff(before, after): a list of records [field, was, now] sorted by field, for the fields whose values differ (if a field is in only one of the dicts, the missing value is None).
tasks.hint: Merge the keys and compare the values with get.

tasks.title: Rate limiting
tasks.statement: Login attempts are an increasing list of seconds. The limit: at most limit attempts in any window seconds (window [t − window + 1, t]). Write allowed_attempts(times, limit, window): a list of True/False for each attempt, whether it is allowed (rejected attempts also count in the window as attempts).
tasks.hint: For each attempt, count the attempts in the window, including itself.

tasks.title: Access rules
tasks.statement: Rules are a list [type, database, role, network, decision]; 'all' means any value, and the network is a CIDR. The first matching rule wins. Write match_rule(rules, db, role, ip, ssl): the decision ('allow' or 'reject') of the first match; the type 'hostssl' matches only when ssl=True, 'host' matches always; if nothing matches, 'reject'. Use ipaddress.
tasks.hint: Go through the rules in order, skipping those that don't match.
